## Summary

Nuclear deformation influences the geometry of the initial state created in
heavy-ion collisions. This presentation explored what happens when the nuclear
shape itself is allowed to fluctuate from event to event, rather than being
described by fixed deformation parameters.

Using analytical estimates and Glauber-model calculations, the study examined
fluctuations of the quadrupole deformation magnitude and triaxiality and their
impact on initial-state observables related to the shape and transverse size of
the collision system. Particular attention was given to how these nuclear-shape
fluctuations modify the moments and correlations of the eccentricity and
inverse transverse size.

The results illustrate how high-energy heavy-ion collisions can provide
sensitivity not only to the average deformation of a nucleus, but also to
fluctuations around its equilibrium shape, providing a connection between
nuclear-structure physics and experimentally accessible collective observables.
